results.finding: Autoantibody-mediated presynaptic NMJ disorders show substantial overlap with paraneoplastic syndromes, particularly with small-cell lung cancer; anti-SOX1 antibodies have higher positivity rates in tumor-associated presentations than in primary autoimmune disease, while anti-VGCC P/Q-type antibodies are positive in >90% of cases regardless of etiology; presynaptic NMJ symptoms can predate radiographic tumor detection by up to 2 years, justifying systematic chest imaging at diagnosis and during follow-up.
results.title: Presynaptic neuromuscular junction disorders: distinguishing paraneoplastic from primary autoimmune etiology

results.finding: A history of one treated lung malignancy does not exclude development of a second primary lung tumor of a different histological subtype; FDG PET-CT is more sensitive than conventional contrast-enhanced CT for detecting occult thoracic malignancy in patients with suspected paraneoplastic neuromuscular syndromes.
results.title: Prior malignancy in the evaluation of a new presynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder

prohibited_recommendations: Do NOT diagnose this as myasthenia gravis based on fatigable weakness alone — RNS facilitation pattern and anti-VGCC positivity place this in the LEMS category.

differential.key_features: MG can produce fatigable weakness but typically shows decrement (not increment) on RNS and normal baseline CMAP; here baseline CMAP low with >100% facilitation at 50 Hz and AChR negative.
Inflammatory myopathy raises CK and shows myopathic EMG; here CK normal and RNS facilitation is diagnostic of pre-synaptic NMJ disorder.
Could explain mild reduced SNAPs but does not produce >100% facilitation on RNS or proximal weakness improving with brief exercise.
Botulism is acute, descending, with autonomic features and bulbar involvement; this is sub-acute over months without an exposure.
Patient is anticoagulated but not on a statin; CK normal.

key_clinical_evidence: LEMS is the principal MG mimic the case is designed to test — pre-synaptic NMJ failure with low baseline CMAP and high-rate facilitation is the discriminator.
Anti-VGCC P/Q-type antibody is positive in 85-90% of LEMS; anti-SOX1 raises paraneoplastic concern for SCLC.
Smoker with prior NSCLC: standard CT may miss small SCLC; PET-CT is essential.
Patient improves with brief exercise (post-activation facilitation) — the opposite pattern to MG; this clinical sign is highly specific.
Treat the underlying SCLC and use amifampridine for symptomatic control; IVIG and immunosuppression are second-line.

patient.history_present_illness: A 72-year-old former smoker with treated non-small cell lung cancer in remission (squamous cell, stage II, surgery + adjuvant chemotherapy 3 years ago) presented for evaluation of progressive proximal leg weakness over 4 months. He initially noticed difficulty rising from low chairs and climbing stairs approximately 4 months ago. He attributed this to deconditioning after his cancer treatment. Over 2 months, the weakness progressed to difficulty rising from the toilet without the safety rail and climbing stairs required use of the handrail. He denies ptosis or diplopia. His wife reports his voice becomes slightly slurred after dinner conversations lasting more than 20 minutes. He has also had increasing dryness of the mouth over the past 6 months, which he attributed to his medication side effects. He mentioned to his urologist that he had developed erectile dysfunction approximately 6 months ago. He does not have significant sensory symptoms in his hands but notices mild numbness and tingling in his feet. His deep tendon reflexes were noted to be diminished at a recent appointment. He underwent surveillance CT chest 6 weeks ago for his lung cancer remission — reported as no evidence of disease recurrence. He was initially referred to physical therapy for 'deconditioning' without improvement. Oncology attributed his weakness to chemotherapy-related peripheral neuropathy and added B12 supplementation. He was subsequently referred to neurology when a repeat EMG performed by his oncologist showed unexpected findings suggesting possible NMJ involvement in addition to mild sensorimotor neuropathy.
